claim: Consider two binary classifiers evaluated at the same sample size \(N\) and the same actual-positive count \(P\), require all four confusion-matrix cells to be strictly positive, and restrict attention to classifiers with positive association \(TP\,TN>FP\,FN\), equivalently positive Matthews correlation coefficient and positive Cohen kappa. Then no pair of classifiers receives opposite strict rankings from the Matthews correlation coefficient \(M\) and Cohen's kappa \(\kappa\) for \(N\le11\). Weak-order agreement first fails at \(N=10\): at \(P=3\), the tables \((TP,FP,FN,TN)=(1,1,2,6)\) and \((2,3,1,4)\) have the same \(M=1/\sqrt{21}\), while \(\kappa=4/19>1/5\). The strict boundary is \(N=12\), where exactly two unordered reversing pairs occur across all prevalences, and they are global class-label complements. A representative at \(P=4\) is \((2,3,2,5)\) versus \((3,5,1,3)\): both have determinant \(TP\,TN-FP\,FN=4\), but \(\kappa=2/17>1/10\) while \(M=1/\sqrt{70}<1/8\). Writing \(Q=N-P\), \(R=TP+FP\), \(S=N-R\), and \(\Delta=TP\,TN-FP\,FN\), one has \(M=\Delta/\sqrt{PQRS}\) and \(\kappa=2\Delta/(PS+QR)\). Thus the first positive-score rank reversal is driven purely by different predicted-class margins even after sample size and true prevalence are fixed.
integrity: The proof uses the exact identities \(M=\Delta/\sqrt{PQRS}\) and \(\kappa=2\Delta/(PS+QR)\). The packaged verifier enumerates all positive-determinant tables through the sharp total and checks every same-prevalence pair without floating-point comparison.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to binary confusion matrices with all four cells positive, common sample size, common actual prevalence, and positive association. It identifies a finite ordinal boundary and does not prescribe a universally preferable performance metric. Cohen's original paper was verified only to month precision in the checked source, so its unresolved exact day is not used as the metadata date anchor.
title: Twelve cases are the sharp positive-score MCC–kappa ranking boundary
